output.brief:
The most likely cause is contaminated brake fluid, not driver technique, the new pads or the hills. Northfield Motor Services serviced 13 Eastgate vans during the bay closure. Eleven of them account for all the soft-pedal complaints. Most used fluid from an old bulk drum that had its cap missing. Two vans got fluid from a fresh drum and have no complaints. Northfield tested two returned vans and found fluid boiling at about 150°C, against 255°C for sealed stock. Fluid that has taken on water can vaporise on long descents, and that fits "fine at the top, long pedal at the bottom". The same drivers logged 604 days in other vans, 141 of them on Upper Wend, with no brake reports. The Calder Road vans carried the same pads and ran the same routes with no complaints. Northfield's 25 Sep recommendation to recheck the other vans got no reply.

What to do this week: pull every Northfield-serviced van, test the fluid and renew it from sealed stock. Drop the warnings and retraining, because they would punish the people who reported a real fault and discourage further reporting. Hold the pad supplier decision, since the squeal data is confounded by fresh pads. I'm fairly sure of this. I have not seen test results on the other vans.
